subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for all legacy ownerless rows, or should upgrades provide a doctor/operator migration path before enforcement?
rationale: The foreign-owner defect has a clear fix, but denying all previously shipped ownerless persisted rows is a security-versus-compatibility policy choice that source inspection cannot safely settle.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows and explicitly accept the compatibility break as the intended security boundary.

options.title: Add migration path
options.body: Provide a doctor-owned migration or explicit operator adoption flow before enforcing owner equality on legacy rows.

options.title: Limit this patch
options.body: Fix foreign-owner mutations now but leave ownerless-row behavior unchanged until a separate migration policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Fail closed
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows and explicitly accept the compatibility break as the intended security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent merged work owns adjacent core session normalization and plugin-boundary behavior, and prior issue triage routed this security choice to him.
